text: Hermes. I walk the dead down here. You're my third today, and I'm already late for the fourth.
how: warm but brisk, a busy man being polite; slight rueful sigh on 'already late'

text: Down where? What is this place? What am I supposed to do?
how: dazed, the questions tumbling out faster and faster

text: All very good questions. I'd love to answer them. I'd also love a day off.
how: dry, kindly, a little smile; deadpan on 'a day off'

text: See the sailor by the water, mending a net? That's Elpenor. He's been here longer than the sand. He'll tell you how it all works.
how: pointing, quicker now, reassuring; a fond tease on 'longer than the sand'

text: Just like that. Somewhere up there, a man is trying to pat a lion. Good luck, Mikon. I mean it. And from now on, chew.
how: already walking off, calling back over his shoulder; sincere on 'I mean it', then a parting wink on 'chew'

text: Careful, you're standing on my net. No, it's fine, it's seen worse. I'm Elpenor. I rowed for Odysseus. Well, near Odysseus. There were a lot of us.
how: young, wry, friendly; still working the net, glances up; self-deprecating correction on 'near Odysseus'

text: And let me guess. He pointed at me and ran. He always leaves the speech to me. Fine. Here's how it works.
how: amused, long-suffering; a theatrical sigh before 'Fine', then settling in to explain

text: Right. Nobody's given you the speech yet. Here's how it works.
how: matter-of-fact, kind, settling in to explain

text: That's the Styx. That's the ferry. The cheerful one on board is Charon. One coin a passenger, no exceptions. Your family were meant to put one under your tongue.
how: tour-guide patter he's done a hundred times; heavy sarcasm on 'the cheerful one'

text: Everyone on this beach has a family that forgot. No coin, you wait a hundred years. I've seen people beg him, bribe him, cry at him. He just flicks water at them.
how: gentle, then dry; deadpan on the last line

text: How long have you been waiting?
Long enough to take up a hobby. Nets. Strange thing to make on a river with no fish in it, but it keeps the hands busy.
how: wry, lifting the net a little; a hint of sadness under the joke

text: So it's a hundred years, or nothing?
Well. There is one other way. It's a terrible idea, so naturally I've thought about it a lot.
how: leaning in, conspiratorial; the grin of a sailor who loves a bad plan
